segments.he: ר' נתן היה מנהגו בבין המצרים לומר קינות בטלית ותפילין והיה אומר בחצות היום חצות במרתף עמוק בבכיות ושפיכת לב עד הערב (כי אמר פעם אחד שאינו יכול לקרר דעתו רק כל השנה בחצות לילה באמירת תיקון חצות שמזה הוא מתעורר בבכיה ושפיכת לב עד שהיה מקרר דעתו) ובין המצרים ותשעה באב בהקינות ובל"א בזה"ל ??? בערב תשעה באב מחצות היום היה סוגר את עצמו במרתף עמוק והיה סגור ומסוגר שם בבכיות ויללות וקולות משונות עד תשעה באב אחר חצות היום כך היה מנהגו כל שנה ושנה לאחר פטירת רבינו ז"ל ולא היה מקרר דעתו עד שהיה רואה את רבינו ז"ל והרב ר' שמואל יצחק מטשערין ז"ל שהיה מגדולי תלמידי רבינו ז"ל היה פ"א עם ר' נתן ז"ל בתשעה באב והוא עשה מנהגו הנ"ל ושמעו את היללות שלו ואח"כ שיצא מהמרתף בלב תקוה מתבהל הר' שמואל יצחק מפניו ואמר [לא מובל 4 מילים] את רבינו ז"ל ואמר שלא הכיר כ"כ את גדולתו עד השנה הזאת
segments.en: Once when Rabbainu was still in his youth in Medvedevka and was fasting many fasts as told in Sichos HaRan — fasting from Shabbos to Shabbos — once in the middle of the week, on the night of the third or fourth day, Rabbainu became very weak and blood poured greatly from his nostrils and mouth. Reb Chaykel begged him to break his fast until Rabbainu was compelled to agree. Reb Chaykel went immediately, took a fowl and had it slaughtered — and right on the way back plucked all the feathers on the road so it would be ready quickly — and cooked it and brought the broth before Rabbainu. [And the full story of the singing of Meyin Olam Haba all night follows as described in story 16 above.] And this Reb Chaykel once asked at the holy grave of Rabbainu — since one has no tzelem Elokim [Divine image] without completing the entire Talmud — that all his descendants should complete the Talmud.

segments.he: ור' נחמן מטולטשין ז"ל בתשעה באב בלילה וביום עד חצות לא דיבר שום דיבור עם שום איש ולא למד מדרש עם העולם כמנהג העולם כי אמר שתשעה באב הוא כמו אבל רח"ל ואבל אסור לדבר כי הוא זה
segments.en: Once in the beginning of Reb Naftali's drawing close to Rabbainu, he had a certain disagreement — Rabbainu said something and Reb Naftali disputed it. Rabbainu replied: "You are not seeing correctly." And immediately Reb Naftali's eyes began to trouble him — and he understood this was a punishment from Rabbainu. He began working to request of Rabbainu that he receive healing for his eyes. When he was before Rabbainu, Rabbainu told him to go to his steward and take a certain book — and he would see inside that it was as Rabbainu had said. He went immediately — and his eyes were healed and he was able to take the book — and Rabbainu showed him as described. Nonetheless in his final days he suffered with his eyes — and Moharan'as wrote him words of rebuke, for Rabbainu had clearly meant his words about doctors for his eyes as well, as cited in Alim LeTrufah.

segments.he: והרב הק' מבארדיטשוב ז"ל היה לובש השטריימל בערב תשעה באב ומצפה ומחכה קרוב לצאת הכוכבים שיבא משיח שיצא לקראתו וכשהגיע ועדין לא בא היה משליך מעליו הבגדים הללו והיה משליך עצמו לארץ ובוכה וצועק השי"ת ישלח לנו את משיח צדקינו בב"א
segments.en: Similarly there was a story at the home of the holy Tzaddik of Berdichev: the Rav of Vilednik, when he was still a young boy, was at the Rav of Berdichev's and debated with him about a Talmudic matter, not wanting to acknowledge the truth. The Rav of Berdichev said: "You are still a young lad and have no sense!" — and, G-d forbid, something happened to his mind. Afterward when Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl was in Berdichev, they brought the young man to him for help. He took him among all the people, stood him on a piece of wood, and told him to sing a melody of the Tzaddik of Berdichev — for the young Reb of Vilednik had spent much time at the Tzaddik of Berdichev's and knew all his melodies beautifully. He sang a melody until his face glistened with sweat. Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl wiped his face with a handkerchief and said: "The Berdichever Rav has mercy on him." And so with several more melodies — each time wiping the sweat and saying the same. And he was healed. But the mark remained with him — for when he later became the Rav and Admor in Vilednik, he was a very great ascetic who could not bear even the smell of a woman. And Reb Gershon of Vilednik of our fellowship was his companion and his person — and would sleep in his room — and was to him literally his entire life-force, for he cherished him above all his people.

segments.he: שמעתי שאחר פטירת רבינו ז"ל השבת הראשון היו תלמידי רבינו ז"ל בבית רבינו ז"ל ואמר ר' יודל שהוא ישב על הכיסא כי יש לו השטריימל של רבינו ז"ל וכן עוד אחרים ענהו מוהרנ"ת ז"ל ואמר שהוא ישב על הכיסא כי הוא יש לו התפילין המוחין (כי היו תפילין של רבינו ז"ל כי פ"א נסע עם רבינו בדרך וביקש רבינו ז"ל שיתן לו התפילין של ר"ת שלו(דהיינו של מוהרנ"ת ז"ל ) ולבש אותם רבינו ז"ל ואח"כ החזירם לו) וישב מוהרנ"ת ז"ל על הכיסא ואמר הזמירות ואמר כשבאו לרבינו זז"ל היה יושב מוהרנ"ת ז"ל בצד אחד ור' נפתלי בצד השני ורבינו ז"ל אמר הזמירות אזמר בשבחין חרוז ור' נתן ור' נפתלי חרוז שני וכן הלאה "ונזמין לה השתא וכו' וכן הלאה עד סוף הזמר ופניו של מוהרנ"ת היו לוהטים כאש לוהט ויצא הרב המגיד מטיראוויצע ז"ל מתוך השולחן ואמר בהתלהבות חשבתי שזה ר' נתן לבסוף אני רואה שזה רבינו בעצמו
segments.en: Once a poor man came to the town of the Gaon the Chasam Sofer. He went to the administrators of the house of study and they gave him meal tickets to eat — one day at this householder's home, one day at that one's, and for Shabbos a ticket to eat at the Chasam Sofer's home. He took the ticket and walked through the street — and encountered the Chasam Sofer himself [not knowing this was the man]. He asked him: "At this man's house — do they give good food?" He replied: "At this man's house they give fish very well." Afterward when he came to the Chasam Sofer's home for Shabbos — and the Chasam Sofer did not recognize him as the one who had asked — they began serving fish. He thought nothing more than fish would be served — so he ate a great deal of the fish, especially since they served many portions. Afterward when they brought the other courses and dishes he could no longer eat at all — for he was completely full. He began to be angry and curse the man who had told him they only give fish. The Chasam Sofer asked why he was angry. He told the story — that he had met a man who answered about the fish — and therefore he had eaten so much fish that he could not eat the other good things. The Chasam Sofer replied: "You yourself are to blame — for why were you such a glutton and covetous person as to ask whether they give good food? And I am the one who answered you about the fish — specifically so that you should learn not to be a glutton."

segments.he: וכן היה בשבועות הגדול אצל מוהרנ"ת ז"ל על שבועות וראה ההתעוררות וכו' (ומוהרנ"ת ז"ל אמר בעצמו על השבועות הזה שהיתקרא שבועות הגדול כי היו שמונים אורחים מלבד אנשי העיירה והיה התעוררות גדול מאד ) שצריך להיזהר לראות בשבועות הגדול הזה שלא לעשות העגל כי הלא גם במתן תורה היה שבועות גדול ואח"כ עשו העגל אמר ג"כ שחשב שהיה מוהרנ"ת ז"ל ולבסוף רואה שהוא רבינו ואמר שאם היה יודע כך לא היה נוסע למ''י והיה נישאר אצלו
segments.en: There was another story at the Chasam Sofer's: he had a private minyan of carefully selected men — all ten men were chosen for their righteousness and piety. Once it happened that one of the minyan's members — not himself but his son — began to step back slightly from the proper path. The Chasam Sofer heard of this and did not want that man in his minyan anymore — even though the man himself continued as righteous and pious as before, and only his son had slightly deviated — and even in this the father was likely not at fault and could not have done anything about it. Nonetheless the Chasam Sofer did not want him in his minyan. But he could not think of what to do — for if he removes him, the man will be shamed. Therefore he resolved to dissolve the entire private minyan and go pray in the house of study with the congregation. And so he did: he discontinued his private minyan and prayed in the house of study.
